patients.summary: Thirty-year-old sales representative with hypertension on lisinopril and generalized anxiety on sertraline who joined in 2023 and then had three motor vehicle crashes in 14 months: hemorrhagic shock with coagulopathy (2024), blunt thoracic aortic injury treated with TEVAR (2025), and intraperitoneal bladder rupture repaired (late 2025). Outside records arrive late or not at all; a 1-year aortic CT report is still outstanding.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o man here to establish. Previous primary care elsewhere; records requested today.

HTN: told he had high blood pressure in 2021, started on lisinopril 10 mg then and has been on the same dose since. Doesn't check at home. No headaches, chest pain, palpitations, swelling.

Anxiety: diagnosed with generalized anxiety around early 2020, sertraline 50 mg since. Describes it as mostly controlled - worries about work numbers and money, some trouble shutting his head off at night, no panic attacks. No SI. Never did counseling, not interested right now. Happy with the dose and doesn't want to change anything.

PMH: as above. PSH: tonsils out as a kid (~10), left knee scope with meniscus repair in 2020 after a pickup basketball injury, no problems since.
Meds: lisinopril 10 daily, sertraline 50 daily.
Allergies: penicillin - rash as a child, flat red spots all over.
FHx: father HTN, had an MI at 55. Mother hypothyroid. One sister, healthy.
SHx: regional sales rep, on the road most days covering a territory. Smokes about 10 cigarettes/day, started ~5 yrs ago. Alcohol 2-3 drinks on weekends. No drugs. Single.

Exam: well appearing. BP and HR in flowsheet. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Left knee with healed arthroscopy portals, full ROM, stable. No edema. Mood good, affect full.

GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 3, AUDIT-C 3.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension - at goal on lisinopril 10. Continue. CMP today.
2. Generalized anxiety disorder - mild symptoms, stable on sertraline 50. Continue. Offered therapy referral anytime.
3. Tobacco use - we talked about quitting given his dad's heart attack and his BP. He's not ready yet. Will revisit.
4. Health maintenance - lipids (family history), CBC, HIV and hep C screening today. Flu shot next month when the clinic gets stock. Tdap per old records, will confirm.

Refills sent for both meds, 90-day supply. RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Brandon - your labs from Tuesday look good. Kidney function, liver tests, electrolytes and blood counts are normal. Cholesterol is fine for now. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. The best thing you can do for your heart long term is still the cigarettes - whenever you're ready, I'm ready.

Allergies: penicillin (maculopapular rash).
Surgical history: tonsillectomy in childhood; arthroscopic meniscal repair, left knee, 2020.
Immunizations: Tdap 05/2019.
Social: smoker, about half a pack a day.
Labs on file (2021, 2022): BMP and CBC within normal limits.

Reviewed by PCP. Lists match what he reported. Tdap entered.

Annual exam, 28M.

Interval: no illnesses, no ED visits. Work steady. Still smoking about 10 a day - started in 2018, so ~6 years. Weekend drinks, 2-3. Plays basketball occasionally, knee holds up.

ROS negative: no chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, GI or GU complaints, no mood changes beyond his usual worry.

Exam: BMI ~26. Skin clear. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR without murmur. Abdomen soft, no masses. GU deferred. Extremities normal, no edema. Neuro grossly intact. Calm, good eye contact.

PHQ-9 2. GAD-7 5. AUDIT-C 3.

- GAD: doing well on sertraline 50.
- Tobacco: counseled again. Precontemplative.
- Prevention: flu vaccine today. Declines COVID booster. Lipids were fine last year, repeat next year. Seatbelt and sunscreen talk; he says he usually buckles up.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (abbreviated)
Admitted: 10/17/2024   Discharged: 10/28/2024
Service: Trauma Surgery / Surgical ICU

Mechanism: 28-year-old male, driver, not wearing a seatbelt, in a high-speed collision with heavy intrusion into the driver side.

Arrival: awake and alert, pale and anxious. BP 85/50, HR 128, RR 22, SpO2 96% on room air. Pelvis unstable to compression; pelvic binder placed in the trauma bay. Large ecchymosis over the left flank. Abdomen distended and tender. FAST: free fluid in the abdomen.

Initial labs: Hgb 8.5 g/dL, platelets 95 K, PT 18 sec, aPTT 40 sec, INR 1.6.

Hospital course: massive transfusion protocol activated in the trauma bay with balanced blood products; coagulopathy corrected. Admitted to the surgical ICU for resuscitation and monitoring, then transferred to the floor once hemodynamically stable. Mobilized with PT. Tolerating diet, voiding, pain controlled at discharge.

Discharge diagnoses:
1. Traumatic hemorrhagic shock with acute coagulopathy
2. Contusion, left flank

Past history: essential hypertension, generalized anxiety disorder. Tonsillectomy, left knee meniscal repair.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Discharge medications: resume home lisinopril 10 mg daily and sertraline 50 mg daily. No new prescriptions.
Social: smoker, 10 cigarettes daily for 6 years; alcohol socially on weekends. Sales representative.
Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks.

Received by fax 12/3/2024 in response to records request of 11/5. Operative, imaging and ICU notes not included.

documents.title: Patient call: recent hospitalization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was in a bad car accident 10/17, at the trauma center for 11 days, ICU for part of it. Got home Monday. Says he 'lost a lot of blood' and got transfusions. Feels weak, sore on the left side, walking around the apartment fine. No fever, no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no blood in urine or stool. Taking his usual two meds, nothing new given. Has not been driving. Booked post-hospital visit Tues 11/5 with PCP. We don't have any records yet - he'll sign a release at the visit. Told to call or go to ED for dizziness, fainting, worsening belly pain or bleeding.

events.reason: post-hospital follow-up after motor vehicle crash

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 8 days after discharge from the trauma center. No records yet; history from Brandon.

On 10/17 he was driving home at night on the highway and was hit hard on the driver side. Admits he wasn't wearing his seatbelt. Remembers the ambulance and the trauma bay, being told his blood pressure was low and his blood 'wasn't clotting'. Got multiple transfusions, a belt around his hips, ICU a few days, then the floor. Home 10/28 with his same meds, no new prescriptions. Doesn't know whether he had surgery or what was bleeding - he thinks not but isn't sure.

Now: tired, gets winded on stairs, left side still sore. Eating OK. Down about 4 kg. No lightheadedness on standing. No dark stools or blood in urine. Walking without a limp. Anxious about getting back in a car - worrying more, sleep broken. Has been a passenger only.

Meds: lisinopril 10, sertraline 50, taking both. Allergy: PCN.

Exam: pale-ish but comfortable. Vitals per flowsheet. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness left flank; large yellow-green bruise over left flank fading. No abdominal wall wounds. Pelvis nontender to gentle compression, walks normally. Legs no swelling or calf tenderness.

GAD-7 11 (up from 5). PHQ-9 6. No SI.

A/P:
1. Traumatic hemorrhagic shock with coagulopathy, s/p transfusion - recovering. CBC today to see where his hemoglobin landed. BMP.
2. Left flank contusion - healing.
3. GAD - worse after the crash, understandable. Not keen on changing sertraline; we'll watch it. Behavioral health number given if he wants to talk to someone.
4. HTN - BP okay, continue lisinopril.
5. Smoking - counseled.
6. Seatbelt - had a straight talk. He gets it.

Records request to the trauma center sent today. Recheck 3 months with CBC, sooner if symptoms.

documents.title: Blood count result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is 11.4 - still below normal but that's expected a few weeks after losing that much blood, and it should keep climbing on its own. Kidney tests and potassium are normal. Eat normally, keep walking, and we'll recheck in February. If you get dizzy, short of breath at rest, or notice black stools, call us.

documents.title: RE: Blood count result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thanks. Feeling a little better each day

documents.title: Back to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doc, just an update. Went back to work full time last week, driving the territory again. Was nervous the first couple days but ok now and I wear the belt every time I promise. Still on for Feb 11?

documents.title: RE: Back to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great to hear. Yes, Feb 11 at 3:20 - please do the blood draw at that visit. If the nerves about driving don't settle, tell me and we'll talk about options.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u ~4 months after the October crash.

Discharge summary came in December (reviewed): shock with coagulopathy, massive transfusion, ICU, left flank contusion. No op note or imaging in what they sent.

Feels back to normal. Energy fine, climbing stairs without getting winded. Left side no longer sore. Back at work since early January. Anxiety about driving improving; GAD-7 8. Sleeping better. Taking sertraline and lisinopril daily.

Still smoking 10/day. Not ready to set a date.

Exam: color good. Weight up 3 kg. Lungs clear, heart regular. Flank bruise gone, nontender. Walks normally.

A/P:
- Post-hemorrhage anemia: CBC today, expect normal.
- Left flank contusion: resolved.
- GAD: improving, continue sertraline 50.
- HTN: fine on lisinopril 10.
- Tobacco: counseled.
RTC for physical in September.

documents.title: CBC result

documents.body: Blood count is back to normal - hemoglobin fully recovered. No iron or anything else needed. See you in the fall.

REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 06/12/2025

CC: chest pain, short of breath after MVC.

HPI: 29M, restrained driver in a high-speed collision, airbags deployed. Arrives by EMS complaining of acute chest pain and trouble breathing. Admitted here 10/2024 for hemorrhagic shock after a prior crash. Hx hypertension and generalized anxiety.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
PSH: tonsillectomy, L knee meniscal repair.
FHx: father with HTN and MI at 55; mother hypothyroid; sister healthy.
SHx: smokes 10 cig/day; social alcohol on weekends; sales rep.

Vitals on arrival: BP 145/90, HR 110, RR 22.

Exam: alert, uncomfortable. Contusion over the sternum. Breath sounds decreased on the left. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvis stable. Moves all extremities.

Labs: Hgb 13.2, Hct 39%, WBC 12,000, Plt 250,000.
CXR: widened mediastinum, left pleural effusion, no rib fractures.
FAST: negative for intra-abdominal fluid.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ischemic changes.
CTA chest: injury of the proximal descending thoracic aorta with mediastinal hematoma; left effusion.

ED course: trauma and vascular surgery at bedside. Taken for endovascular repair.

Impression: blunt thoracic aortic injury after MVC.
Disposition: admitted to trauma surgery / vascular surgery, to the OR.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/12/2025   Discharged 06/17/2025

Principal diagnosis: blunt thoracic aortic injury, proximal descending thoracic aorta.

Procedure 06/12/2025: thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) with stent graft, percutaneous right femoral access, vascular surgery.

Course: uncomplicated repair. Monitored overnight in the ICU, then the floor. Left pleural effusion followed on exam and imaging, not drained. Right groin access site without hematoma. Ambulating, eating, pain controlled. Discharged home.

Allergies: penicillin.
Discharge medications: continue lisinopril 10 mg daily and sertraline 50 mg daily. No changes.
Instructions: no heavy lifting for 2 weeks; no driving while sore. Stop smoking.
Follow-up: vascular surgery clinic with CT angiogram in 1 month. Primary care in 1-2 weeks.

ED record and discharge summary received together by fax 07/08/2025.

documents.title: Another accident
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I hate to say it but I was in another crash last week, the 12th. I was wearing my belt this time. They found a tear in my aorta and fixed it with a stent through my groin, I was in 5 days and got home Tuesday. They said see my doctor in 1-2 weeks. Can I get in? Chest is sore but breathing is fine now.

documents.title: RE: Another accident
documents.author: RN
documents.body: So sorry to hear this, Brandon. You're booked Tuesday 6/24 at 10:40 with your doctor. If you get new chest or back pain, shortness of breath, a swelling or bleeding at the groin, or a cold or numb leg before then, go to the ED. Please sign the records release we just sent so we can get the hospital notes.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 7 days after discharge. Hospital records not here yet; requested.

Per Brandon: 6/12, belted, airbags went off, high speed. Chest pain and couldn't catch his breath at the scene. At the trauma center they found an injury to his aorta on CT and repaired it the same night with a stent graft through the right groin. 5 days in, ICU one night. Discharged on his same two meds.

Now: chest wall sore where the airbag hit, better daily. Breathing comfortable. No back pain. Groin a little bruised, no swelling. Walking a mile a day. No fevers. Not driving yet.

Anxiety up again - 'what are the odds, twice'. GAD-7 9. Sleeping OK most nights. Declines a dose change or counseling for now.

Exam: comfortable. Healing yellow bruise over sternum, mildly tender. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Right groin puncture site healed, no hematoma or bruit. Femoral and pedal pulses intact both sides. No leg swelling.

A/P:
1. Blunt thoracic aortic injury s/p TEVAR 6/12 - recovering. Vascular follow-up with CTA in a month already scheduled. Explained why BP control and stopping smoking matter for the graft.
2. HTN - continue lisinopril 10.
3. GAD - flare after the crash, continue sertraline 50, revisit at the physical.
4. Tobacco - he says he'll cut down. Counseled.
CBC, BMP today. RTC at the physical in September.

documents.title: Labs after hospital stay
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts and kidney function normal. Good news after the procedure and the contrast dye. Nothing to change.

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast, compared with 06/12/2025. Thoracic aortic stent graft in the proximal descending aorta in good position. No endoleak. Mediastinal hematoma decreased in size. Left pleural effusion has resolved. Lungs clear. Heart and pericardium normal.
reports.conclusion: Stent graft in good position without endoleak. Decreasing mediastinal hematoma. Left effusion resolved.

documents.title: Vascular Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Vascular Surgery Clinic - Date of visit 07/17/2025

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Slattery one month after thoracic endovascular repair of a blunt aortic injury (06/12/2025, right femoral access). He feels well. Chest wall soreness nearly gone. No back pain, no claudication, no groin problems.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily. Allergy: penicillin (rash).
Smoking: continues, about 10 per day.

Exam: right groin access site well healed. Femoral and distal pulses normal bilaterally.

CTA chest today: graft in good position, no endoleak, mediastinal hematoma smaller, left effusion resolved.

Impression: satisfactory early result after TEVAR.

Recommendations: keep blood pressure well controlled; we strongly recommend he stop smoking. Repeat CT angiogram at 1 year, here. No activity restrictions now.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast, followed by CT cystogram with dilute contrast instilled through the urethral catheter. Contrast extravasates from the bladder dome into the peritoneal cavity, outlining bowel loops. Free fluid in the pelvis and both paracolic gutters. Liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys and adrenals without injury. No hydronephrosis. Thoracic aortic stent graft partially imaged, unchanged. No acute fracture.
reports.conclusion: Intraperitoneal bladder rupture at the dome. No solid-organ injury.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 12/19/2025

CC: lower abdominal pain, can't urinate.

HPI: 30M, restrained driver in a head-on MVC about 3 hours ago. Severe pain low in the abdomen since; has not passed any urine since the crash. Known to us: hemorrhagic shock after an MVC 10/2024; blunt aortic injury 6/2025 repaired with TEVAR. HTN, GAD.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
SHx: smoker, 10/day; weekend alcohol.

Vitals: BP 110/70, HR 102, RR 22, T 37.1 C.

Exam: alert, in distress from pain. Tender and bruised over the suprapubic area. Abdomen otherwise soft. Pelvis stable. Foley catheter placed - no urine returned.

Labs: BUN 36, creatinine 1.8, K 4.5, Hgb 13.2, WBC 12,000.

CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast and CT cystogram: contrast leaking from the bladder dome into the peritoneum, pelvic free fluid. No solid organ injury. Aortic graft unchanged.

Impression: intraperitoneal bladder rupture. Elevated BUN/creatinine attributed to absorption of urine from the peritoneum.

Disposition: trauma surgery and urology consulted; to the OR for repair. Admitted.

Received by fax 01/14/2026 after second request. Discharge summary not included.

documents.title: Patient call: third crash, bladder repair
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Brandon called. Head-on crash 12/19, belted. Bladder was torn and he had surgery that night through a cut in his belly to sew it up. Home 12/23 with a Foley catheter, urology is taking it out in about 2 weeks after a dye test. Pain controlled. Catheter draining clear yellow urine. No fever. Incision dry. Same two meds. Booked with PCP Tues 12/30. Reviewed reasons to go to ED: fever, catheter stops draining, blood clots, increasing belly pain, redness or drainage at the incision. Records request faxed to the trauma center.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Third post-crash visit in 14 months.

12/19 head-on collision, seatbelt on. Couldn't void afterward, severe low belly pain. Per patient the CT showed a tear at the top of the bladder leaking into the abdomen; laparotomy and repair that night. 4 days inpatient. Home 12/23 with a urethral catheter. Was told his kidney numbers were up when he came in because of the leak. Urology appointment 1/6 for a bladder x-ray and catheter removal. No records yet (requested 12/26).

Now: incision sore, improving. Catheter draining well, clear. No fever or chills. Bowels moving. Eating. Meds unchanged.

Pretty shaken. Talking about whether he can keep doing a job that's all driving. GAD-7 8 - lower than I'd have guessed. No SI.

Exam: uncomfortable getting on the table. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Lower midline incision clean and dry, no redness. Mild suprapubic tenderness. Catheter in place, clear yellow urine in bag. No leg swelling.

A/P:
1. Intraperitoneal bladder rupture s/p repair 12/19 - healing; catheter care reviewed; keep the 1/6 urology visit.
2. Elevated creatinine at admission - recheck BMP today.
3. HTN - stays on lisinopril 10.
4. Blunt aortic injury s/p TEVAR - CTA due 6/2026.
5. GAD - continue sertraline; offered counseling referral again, he'll think about it.
6. Smoking - counseled.
RTC March, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Kidney function
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your creatinine is 0.98 - normal. The high number in the ED was from the urine leaking into your belly, not kidney damage. Blood count fine too. Happy new year, and good luck on the 6th.

documents.title: Catheter out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good news, catheter came out yesterday. They did the dye x-ray first and said the bladder healed, no leak. Peeing on my own fine. Urology said they'd send you a note.

documents.title: RE: Catheter out
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news. Call us if you get burning, fever, trouble emptying, or blood in the urine. I'll note it in your chart and look out for their note.

documents.title: Records follow-up: trauma center
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called trauma center HIM re: 12/26 request for the 12/19-12/23 admission. Told it is in the queue. Re-faxed the request and signed release. Also asked urology office for the 1/6 visit note - they will send when signed.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My manager needs a note that I can go back to driving the territory starting Feb 2. Surgeon cleared me already. Can you write one?

documents.body:
To whom it may concern,

Brandon Slattery is under my care. He may return to his usual duties, including driving, as of February 2, 2026, without restrictions.

Please contact our office with questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine f/u, BP and anxiety; first visit since the bladder repair.

ED record from 12/19 came in January (CT: intraperitoneal rupture at the dome, BUN 36 / Cr 1.8 on arrival). Still no discharge summary or op note, and nothing from urology. Per him the 1/6 cystogram showed no leak and the catheter came out.

GU: voiding normally, good stream, no burning or blood, no leaking, empties fully. Incision healed.
Back at work since Feb 2. Driving fine, he says, belt on.
HTN: no symptoms. On lisinopril 10.
GAD: GAD-7 6, PHQ-9 3. Doing better than he expected after the winter.
Smoking: same, 10/day. Not ready.

Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, healed lower midline scar, nontender. No edema.

A/P:
1. Intraperitoneal bladder rupture s/p repair - healed per urology, asymptomatic. Resolved.
2. HTN - continue lisinopril 10. BMP.
3. Blunt thoracic aortic injury s/p TEVAR - 1-yr CTA with vascular in June.
4. GAD - stable, sertraline 50.
5. Tobacco - counseled.
BP/smoking check in May, physical in September.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium normal. See you in May.

documents.body: Had my 1 year CT for the aorta stent on Thursday 6/18. The vascular surgeon told me it looks stable. FYI.

documents.body: Thanks for letting me know - glad it looks good. We don't have the report yet, so our front desk will request it from the vascular office.
